Friction Interventions Effectively Reduce Social Media Use Independent of Users’ Susceptibility

2026-11-02

1 Abstract

Many young people use social media more than they intend, and social media platforms are criticized for designing seamless interfaces to maximize engagement. Adding friction at app opening is considered a promising approach to reduce usage and improve social media well-being, yet it remains unclear whether such access frictions work equally well for different users. Drawing on the Differential Susceptibility to Media Effects Model, this study examines (1) whether access friction interventions reduce social media use and improve social media well-being, and (2) whether their efficacy varies by age, fear of missing out (FOMO), and ostracism. In a six-week randomized controlled field experiment with adolescents and emerging adults in Germany (N = 484, Mage = 19.05, SDage = 2.31), we compared two access friction interventions, a delay and a session time planning prompt at app opening, against a control condition. We studied the effects on usage (daily app openings, dismissal of app use, and rapid checking) and social media well-being (social media satisfaction and problematic use). Findings revealed that both interventions led users to be more likely to dismiss app use and reduced the number of daily app openings. The delay reduced rapid checking behavior, and time planning prompts increased social media satisfaction. Contrary to the assumption that effects depend on user susceptibility, age, FOMO, and ostracism did not moderate these effects, suggesting that access friction is a broadly applicable tool for reducing social media use and, to a limited extent, improving social media well-being.

2 About this script

This script reproduces all analyses of the paper from three files: the one sec log, the pre-survey, and the post-survey. It includes: data preparation, measures, descriptive results, the three research questions, an appendix with robustness checks, and the model diagnostics at the end. Section names refer to the tables and figures of the paper.

The conditions are called Control, Waiting, and Planning in the data and control, waiting prompts, and time planning prompts in the paper. Control is the reference condition in all models.

3 Helper functions

z-scores, APA formatting of numbers and tables, extraction of coefficients, model comparisons for the moderation analyses, and the figure style.

# --- General ----------------------------------------------------------------
z_score <- function(x) {
  (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

outcomes_a <- c("social_media_satisfaction", "prob_self")
subj_label <- c(
  social_media_satisfaction = "Social media satisfaction",
  prob_self = "Problematic use"
)

# --- APA table formatting (gt) ----------------------------------------------
stars <- function(p) {
  as.character(cut(p, c(-Inf, .001, .01, .05, Inf), c("***", "**", "*", "")))
}
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, p) {
  sprintf("%.2f%s [%.2f, %.2f]", est, stars(p), lo, hi)
}
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
# Values bounded to |1| (correlations, ICC): APA drops the leading zero; the
# sign (if any) is kept.
fmt_r <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
}

# APA-style gt renderer
gt_apa <- function(data, title, subtitle = NULL, note = NULL,
                   stub = NULL, left_cols = NULL) {
  g <- gt(data, rowname_col = stub) |>
    tab_header(
      title = md(sprintf("**%s**", title)),
      subtitle = if (!is.null(subtitle)) md(sprintf("*%s*", subtitle))
    ) |>
    sub_missing(missing_text = "") |>
    cols_align("center", columns = everything())
  if (!is.null(left_cols)) {
    g <- cols_align(g, "left", columns = all_of(left_cols))
  }
  if (!is.null(note)) {
    g <- tab_source_note(g, md(sprintf("*Note.* %s", note)))
  }
  g |>
    opt_align_table_header(align = "left") |>
    tab_options(
      table.border.top.style = "none",
      table.border.bottom.style = "none",
      heading.border.bottom.style = "none",
      column_labels.border.top.style = "solid",
      column_labels.border.top.width = px(2),
      column_labels.border.top.color = "black",
      column_labels.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(1),
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
      table_body.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      table_body.border.bottom.width = px(2),
      table_body.border.bottom.color = "black",
      table_body.hlines.style = "none",
      stub.border.style = "none",
      table.font.names = "Times New Roman",
      table.font.size = px(13),
      data_row.padding = px(3),
      source_notes.font.size = px(11)
    )
}

# --- Coefficient / fit tables -----------------------------------------------
short_term <- function(v) {
  v <- gsub("condWaiting", "Waiting prompts", v)
  v <- gsub("condPlanning", "Time planning prompts", v)
  v <- gsub("wavepost", "post", v)
  v <- gsub("age_z", "age", v)
  v <- gsub("fomo_z", "FOMO", v)
  v <- gsub("ostracism_z", "ostr", v)
  v
}

# Usage (glmmTMB) coefficients as ratios (IRR/OR) with Wald 95% CI.
coef_glmm <- function(model, label) {
  co <- summary(model)$coefficients$cond
  est <- co[, "Estimate"]
  se <- co[, "Std. Error"]
  out <- data.frame(
    ratio = round(exp(est), 3),
    lo = round(exp(est - 1.96 * se), 3),
    hi = round(exp(est + 1.96 * se), 3),
    p = round(co[, "Pr(>|z|)"], 4),
    row.names = short_term(rownames(co))
  )
  cat("\n---", label, "---\n")
  print(out)
}
fit_glmm <- function(model, label) {
  vc <- VarCorr(model)$cond
  tibble(
    outcome = label,
    rand_sd = paste(
      sprintf(
        "%s=%.2f",
        names(vc),
        vapply(vc, \(x) as.numeric(attr(x, "stddev")), numeric(1))
      ),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    AIC = round(AIC(model), 1),
    BIC = round(BIC(model), 1),
    N = stats::nobs(model)
  )
}

# Social media well-being (lmer) coefficients as unstandardized b with Wald 95% CI.
coef_lmm <- function(model, label) {
  co <- summary(model)$coefficients
  est <- co[, "Estimate"]
  se <- co[, "Std. Error"]
  pcol <- if ("Pr(>|t|)" %in% colnames(co)) "Pr(>|t|)" else ncol(co)
  out <- data.frame(
    beta = round(est, 3),
    lo = round(est - 1.96 * se, 3),
    hi = round(est + 1.96 * se, 3),
    p = round(co[, pcol], 4),
    row.names = short_term(rownames(co))
  )
  cat("\n---", label, "---\n")
  print(out)
}
fit_lmm <- function(model, label) {
  rand <- if (inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    v <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
    paste(sprintf("%s=%.2f", v$grp, v$sdcor), collapse = "; ")
  } else {
    "-"
  }
  tibble(
    outcome = label, rand_sd = rand,
    AIC = round(AIC(model), 1), BIC = round(BIC(model), 1),
    N = stats::nobs(model)
  )
}

# --- Moderated vs non-moderated model comparison ----------------------------
# Change in fit when a moderation block is added: moderated minus
# non-moderated model (ML fits; negative values favor the moderated model).
fit_delta <- function(reduced, full) {
  tibble(
    d_aic = AIC(full) - AIC(reduced),
    d_bic = BIC(full) - BIC(reduced)
  )
}
# Refit a model without the moderation terms and compare.
drop_fit <- function(full, drop_terms) {
  rhs <- paste0(". ~ . - ", paste(drop_terms, collapse = " - "))
  fit_delta(update(full, as.formula(rhs)), full)
}

# --- Usage moderation model -------------------------------------------------
build_openings <- function(mod) {
  glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste0(
      "openings ~ cond * ", mod,
      " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id) + (1 | app)"
    )),
    family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
    data = openings_daily,
    control = ctrl
  )
}
build_dismissal <- function(mod) {
  glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste0(
      "dismissed ~ cond * ", mod,
      " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id) + (1 | app)"
    )),
    family = binomial(),
    data = dismissal_ev,
    control = ctrl
  )
}
build_rate <- function(mod) {
  glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste0(
      "burst_rate ~ cond * ", mod,
      " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id)"
    )),
    family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
    data = burst_daily,
    control = ctrl
  )
}

# --- Social media well-being moderation model -------------------------------
prepost_fit <- function(d, mod) {
  lmer(
    as.formula(paste0("value ~ wave * cond * ", mod, " + (1 | match_id)")),
    data = d, REML = FALSE
  )
}
prepost_mod <- function(rhs, oc) {
  lmer(
    as.formula(paste0("value ~ ", rhs, " + (1 | match_id)")),
    data = filter(survey_long, outcome == oc), REML = FALSE
  )
}

# --- Usage effect ratios (figures) ------------------------------------------
ratio_eff <- function(model, label) {
  df <- emmeans(model, ~ cond) |>
    contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, type = "response", adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  # log-link models name the column "ratio"; the logistic model "odds.ratio".
  rc <- intersect(c("ratio", "odds.ratio"), names(df))[1]
  tibble(
    outcome = label,
    condition = factor(c("Waiting", "Planning"), levels = c("Planning",
      "Waiting")),
    est = df[[rc]], lo = df$asymp.LCL, hi = df$asymp.UCL
  )
}

# --- ICC / effect-size helpers (social media well-being) --------------------
icc_uncond <- function(d) {
  m0 <- lmer(value ~ 1 + (1 | match_id), data = d)
  v <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m0))
  vp <- v$vcov[v$grp == "match_id"]
  ve <- v$vcov[v$grp == "Residual"]
  round(vp / (vp + ve), 3)
}

# --- Figure palette and theme ----------------------------------------------
col_control <- "#737373"
col_waiting <- "#8dadbf"
col_planning <- "#9e0b1d"
cond_colours <- c(Control = col_control, Waiting = col_waiting,
  Planning = col_planning)
# Display labels for the conditions (levels stay Control/Waiting/Planning).
cond_labels <- c(Control = "Control", Waiting = "Waiting prompts",
  Planning = "Time planning prompts")
fig_font <- "sans"

theme_house <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = fig_font) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "black"),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(colour = "black"),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = base_size),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = base_size - 1),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# Condition-on-y effect panel for one outcome. Ratios (IRR/OR) are shown on a
# log scale around 1, standardized effects (d) on a linear scale around 0.
eff_panel <- function(eff_df, xlab, title, ref = 1, log_x = TRUE) {
  eff_df |>
    ggplot(aes(est, condition, colour = condition)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref, linewidth = 0.6, colour = "black") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0.18,
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    # White box behind the value, so the reference line does not run through
    # labels of effects close to it (e.g., d = 0.01).
    geom_label(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", est)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3.6,
      colour = "black", fill = "white", label.size = 0,
      label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colours, labels = cond_labels) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = cond_labels) +
    (if (log_x) scale_x_log10() else scale_x_continuous()) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_house()
}

4 Data preparation

The one sec app logged each completed opening and each dismissal with a timestamp and the target application. This section turns the log data and the two surveys into the analysis frames: one row per participant, app, and day for daily openings; one row per decision point for dismissal of app use; one row per participant and day for bursts of use; and one row per participant, outcome, and wave for the survey outcomes.

4.1 Import and IDs

This section links the log and the surveys via the anonymized identifier, and removes test accounts and accounts with fewer than two events. Three participants submitted the post-survey twice. One submission per person is kept.

behavior <- read_csv2(
  "behavior_data_set_5.csv",
  col_types = cols(suggestionLearnMoreLinkTapped = col_character())
) |>
  clean_names()

pre <- read_csv2("pre_survey_data_set_5.csv") |>
  clean_names()
post <- read_csv2("post_survey_data_set_5.csv") |>
  clean_names()

# Satisfaction outcome renamed to the paper's label.
pre <- rename(pre, social_media_satisfaction = social_media_wellbeing)
post <- rename(post, social_media_satisfaction = social_media_wellbeing)

print(count(pre, cond))
## # A tibble: 3 × 2
##   cond               n
##   <chr>          <int>
## 1 control          265
## 2 default          264
## 3 reintervention   263
# Data labels: "control" = Control, "reintervention" = Planning, all other
# labels = Waiting; missing stays NA.
pre <- pre |>
  mutate(
    cond = case_when(
      cond == "control" ~ "Control",
      cond == "reintervention" ~ "Planning",
      !is.na(cond) ~ "Waiting"
    ),
    cond = factor(cond, levels = c("Control", "Waiting", "Planning"))
  )

# Common ID key across the three sources.
behavior <- behavior |>
  mutate(match_id = str_remove(userid, "^.*2024-"))
pre <- pre |>
  mutate(match_id = str_remove(uuid, "^.*2024-"))
post <- post |>
  mutate(match_id = str_remove(uuid, "^.*2024-"))

# Three participants submitted the post-survey twice: keep one submission per
# person, preferring a non-empty one and otherwise the first in the file.
post <- post |>
  arrange(match_id, is.na(social_media_satisfaction) & is.na(prob_self)) |>
  distinct(match_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Drop test accounts, attach condition to the behavioral log.
behavior <- behavior |>
  filter(!str_starts(match_id, "test")) |>
  left_join(pre |> select(match_id, cond), by = "match_id")

# Raw per-person activity before the activity/scope filters
raw_activity <- behavior |>
  count(match_id, name = "n_raw_events")

# Drop ghost accounts (< 2 events).
active_users <- behavior |>
  count(match_id, name = "n_events") |>
  filter(n_events >= 2) |>
  pull(match_id)
behavior <- behavior |>
  filter(match_id %in% active_users)

4.2 Target apps

One sec only intervened on the apps that participants had chosen as target apps. We kept social media platforms on which users mainly view and share content with a wider audience (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, X/Twitter, Pinterest, Facebook, Reddit, BeReal, LinkedIn, Threads, and Jodel) and excluded non-social apps and messengers.

# Harmonize app names (spelling variants of the same app).
behavior <- behavior |>
  mutate(
    app_l = str_to_lower(app),
    app = case_when(
      str_detect(app_l, "tik") ~ "TikTok",
      str_detect(app_l, "insta") ~ "Instagram",
      str_detect(app_l, "snap") ~ "Snapchat",
      str_detect(app_l, "you.?tube|yt") ~ "YouTube",
      str_detect(app_l, "face") ~ "Facebook",
      # Raw data misspells "whastapp".
      str_detect(app_l, "whats|whast") ~ "WhatsApp",
      str_detect(app_l, "pin") ~ "Pinterest",
      str_detect(app_l, "linked") ~ "LinkedIn",
      str_detect(app_l, "twitch") ~ "Twitch",
      str_detect(app_l, "twitter|^x$|x\\.") ~ "X/Twitter",
      str_detect(app_l, "redd") ~ "Reddit",
      str_detect(app_l, "be.?real") ~ "BeReal",
      TRUE ~ str_to_title(app)
    )
  ) |>
  select(-app_l)

# Scope: content-focused social apps only; messaging and non-social apps
# excluded.
social_apps <- c(
  "Instagram", "TikTok", "YouTube", "Snapchat", "X/Twitter",
  "Pinterest", "Facebook", "Reddit", "BeReal", "LinkedIn",
  "Threads", "Jodel"
)
behavior <- behavior |>
  filter(app %in% social_apps)

4.3 Person-level variables

Age, FOMO, and ostracism (without item 5, which is not part of the original scale) from the pre-survey, and whether a person ever triggered the intervention.

# Pre-wave trait means (RQ3b: FOMO; RQ3c: ostracism).
# No reverse-keyed items
pre <- pre |>
  mutate(
    # Ostracism item 5 excluded from every analysis.
    ostracism_mean = rowMeans(
      across(starts_with("ostracism_") & !any_of("ostracism_5")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    fomo_mean = rowMeans(across(starts_with("fomo_")), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

person_cov <- pre |>
  transmute(
    match_id,
    cond,
    age,
    # Only participants aged 13 to 25 enter the analyses.
    age_ok = coalesce(between(age, 13, 25), FALSE),
    ostracism_mean,
    fomo_mean
  )

# Exposure flag: TRUE if the person logged any one sec event before the
# activity/scope filters.
person_cov <- person_cov |>
  left_join(raw_activity, by = "match_id") |>
  mutate(
    n_raw_events = coalesce(n_raw_events, 0L),
    exposed = n_raw_events > 0L
  )

4.4 Local time and repeated openings

Timestamps are converted into the participants’ local time, which defines the date, the weekday, and the study day. Only the six-week intervention period is analyzed (study days 0 to 41 in the code, i.e., days 1 to 42). Repeated openings of the same app within 70 seconds of the initial opening count as a single opening event.

# Timestamps are UTC; date and weekday follow each event's time zone.
behavior <- behavior |>
  mutate(
    timestamp = as_datetime(timestamp),
    tz_local = coalesce(timezone, "Europe/Berlin")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    local_time = force_tz(with_tz(timestamp, first(tz_local)), "UTC"),
    .by = tz_local
  ) |>
  mutate(
    date = as_date(local_time),
    weekend = if_else(
      wday(local_time, week_start = 1) %in% c(6, 7),
      "weekend",
      "weekday"
    ),
    weekend = factor(weekend, levels = c("weekday", "weekend"))
  ) |>
  # Time trend: days since the person's first event.
  mutate(
    study_day = as.integer(date - min(date, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by = match_id
  ) |>
  # Six-week intervention period: study days 0 to 41 (days 1 to 42).
  filter(study_day <= 41)
# Repeated openings of the same app within 70 s count as one.
flag_first_opening <- function(t) {
  keep <- logical(length(t))
  anchor <- -Inf
  for (i in seq_along(t)) {
    if (t[i] - anchor > 70) {
      anchor <- t[i]
      keep[i] <- TRUE
    }
  }
  keep
}

behavior <- behavior |>
  mutate(row_id = row_number())

repeat_opens <- behavior |>
  filter(resolution == "openedApp") |>
  arrange(match_id, app, timestamp) |>
  mutate(
    first_open = flag_first_opening(as.numeric(timestamp)),
    .by = c(match_id, app)
  ) |>
  filter(!first_open) |>
  pull(row_id)

cat("Repeated openings removed:", length(repeat_opens), "\n")
## Repeated openings removed: 7817
behavior <- behavior |>
  filter(!row_id %in% repeat_opens) |>
  select(-row_id)

4.5 Decision points at the end of a self-set limit

In Time planning, a further decision point occurred when the self-set limit had elapsed. Because the experience sampling prompt appeared only when participants tried to open an app, continuations without this prompt within 60 s after the most recent self-set limit for the same app had elapsed, and dismissals within this window, count as decision points at the end of the limit. They enter the analysis for dismissal of app use, but not daily openings or bursts of use. The 60 s window covers the cluster of continuations without a prompt right after a limit ran out.

# End of a self-set limit (Time planning): continuing without an experience
# sampling prompt (no opening reason) or dismissing within 60 s after the most
# recent self-set limit of the same app ran out.
behavior <- behavior |>
  arrange(match_id, app, timestamp) |>
  group_by(match_id, app) |>
  mutate(
    # End of each self-set limit, in seconds
    limit_ends = if_else(
      resolution == "openedApp" &
        !is.na(time_interval_until_re_intervention) &
        time_interval_until_re_intervention > 0,
      as.numeric(timestamp) + time_interval_until_re_intervention,
      NA_real_
    ),
    prev_limit_end = lag(limit_ends)
  ) |>
  fill(prev_limit_end) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    no_esm = resolution == "openedApp" & (is.na(reason) | reason == ""),
    since_limit = as.numeric(timestamp) - prev_limit_end,
    end_of_limit = coalesce(
      cond == "Planning" &
        (no_esm | resolution == "dismissedAppOpening") &
        between(since_limit, 0, 60),
      FALSE
    )
  ) |>
  select(-limit_ends, -prev_limit_end)

behavior |>
  filter(
    cond == "Planning",
    resolution %in% c("openedApp", "dismissedAppOpening")
  ) |>
  count(resolution, no_esm, end_of_limit)
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   resolution          no_esm end_of_limit     n
##   <chr>               <lgl>  <lgl>        <int>
## 1 dismissedAppOpening FALSE  FALSE        17653
## 2 dismissedAppOpening FALSE  TRUE          1502
## 3 openedApp           FALSE  FALSE        44498
## 4 openedApp           TRUE   FALSE         4099
## 5 openedApp           TRUE   TRUE          6449

4.6 Outcomes

From the decision points we derive three outcomes. Daily openings count the completed openings per participant, app, and day with at least one access attempt (0 if all attempts were dismissed). Dismissal of app use codes each decision point as 1 (dismissed) or 0 (continued to the app). Bursts of use are sequences of at least two access attempts (completed or dismissed) within five minutes. The daily burst rate counts them per participant and day with at least one burst. Self-set limits are kept for the descriptives only.

behavior_ev <- behavior |>
  left_join(person_cov |> select(-cond), by = "match_id") |>
  mutate(resolution = factor(resolution))

# Attempts to open an app: all decision points except those at the end of a
# self-set limit (daily openings and bursts of use).
access_ev <- filter(behavior_ev, !end_of_limit)
# DV 1: daily openings per participant x app x day, on days with at least one
# attempt to open an app (0 if all attempts were dismissed).
openings_from <- function(events) {
  events |>
    filter(resolution %in% c("openedApp", "dismissedAppOpening")) |>
    summarise(
      openings = sum(resolution == "openedApp"),
      study_day = first(study_day),
      .by = c(match_id, app, date)
    ) |>
    mutate(
      weekend = if_else(
        wday(date, week_start = 1) %in% c(6, 7),
        "weekend",
        "weekday"
      ),
      weekend = factor(weekend, levels = c("weekday", "weekend"))
    ) |>
    left_join(person_cov, by = "match_id") |>
    filter(age_ok)
}

openings_daily <- openings_from(filter(behavior, !end_of_limit))
# DV 2: dismissal of app use at every decision point (including the end of a
# self-set limit).
dismissal_ev <- behavior_ev |>
  filter(resolution %in% c("openedApp", "dismissedAppOpening")) |>
  mutate(
    cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"),
    dismissed = if_else(resolution == "dismissedAppOpening", 1L, 0L)
  ) |>
  filter(age_ok)
# Self-set session limits (Planning arm)
limit_ev <- behavior_ev |>
  filter(
    cond == "Planning",
    !is.na(time_interval_until_re_intervention)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    limit_sec = time_interval_until_re_intervention
  ) |>
  filter(limit_sec > 0, age_ok)
# DV 3: bursts. A burst is a sequence of at least 2 attempts to open an app 
# less than 5 min apart; a gap longer than 5 min starts a new burst.
# Bursts span apps. The 60 s prompt suppression hides re-checks under 1 minute.
burst_gap_mins <- 5

burst_events <- access_ev |>
  filter(
    resolution %in% c("openedApp", "dismissedAppOpening"),
    age_ok
  ) |>
  arrange(match_id, timestamp) |>
  mutate(
    gap_to_prev = as.numeric(
      difftime(timestamp, lag(timestamp), units = "mins")
    ),
    new_burst = is.na(gap_to_prev) | gap_to_prev > burst_gap_mins,
    burst_id = cumsum(new_burst),
    .by = match_id
  ) |>
  mutate(burst_uid = paste(match_id, burst_id, sep = "_"))

# Burst level: one row per burst, dated by its first event.
burst_level <- burst_events |>
  summarise(
    calendar_date = first(date),
    study_day = first(study_day),
    weekend = first(weekend),
    cond = first(cond),
    age_ok = first(age_ok),
    age = first(age),
    n_events = n(),
    .by = c(match_id, burst_uid)
  ) |>
  # A burst requires at least 2 access events
  filter(n_events >= 2) |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"))

# User-day level: one row per participant-day.
burst_daily <- burst_level |>
  summarise(
    study_day = first(study_day),
    weekend = first(weekend),
    cond = first(cond),
    age_ok = first(age_ok),
    age = first(age),
    burst_rate = n(),
    .by = c(match_id, calendar_date)
  ) |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"))

4.7 Survey outcomes

The participants who reported social media satisfaction and problematic social media use (single items, 1 to 4) at pre and post in a long format (one row per participant, outcome, and survey wave) for the survey wave × condition models.

# Participants who completed both surveys (one row per person).
survey_pp <- pre |>
  select(match_id, cond) |>
  semi_join(post, by = "match_id") |>
  left_join(person_cov |> select(match_id, age, age_ok), by = "match_id") |>
  filter(age_ok)

# Long: for the wave x condition mixed model.
shared_outcomes <- c("social_media_satisfaction", "prob_self")
completers <- intersect(pre$match_id, post$match_id)

survey_long <- bind_rows(
  pre |>
    filter(match_id %in% completers) |>
    select(match_id, all_of(shared_outcomes)) |>
    mutate(wave = "pre"),
  post |>
    filter(match_id %in% completers) |>
    select(match_id, all_of(shared_outcomes)) |>
    mutate(wave = "post")
) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(shared_outcomes), names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "value") |>
  left_join(
    person_cov |> select(match_id, cond, age, age_ok),
    by = "match_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(wave = factor(wave, levels = c("pre", "post"))) |>
  filter(age_ok)

4.8 Frames for the robustness checks

Alternative versions of the openings data, used only in the appendix: without each participant’s first and last active day, and smoothed with a three-day rolling median (= median of that day and its two neighboring days, which smooths extreme days).

# (1) Transition-day trim: drop each user's first and last active day.
user_span <- behavior |>
  group_by(match_id) |>
  summarise(
    first_day = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_day = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

openings_daily_trim <- openings_daily |>
  left_join(user_span, by = "match_id") |>
  filter(date > first_day, date < last_day) |>
  select(-first_day, -last_day)

# (2) Three-day rolling-median openings.
openings_daily_smooth <- openings_daily |>
  select(match_id, app, date, openings) |>
  group_by(match_id, app) |>
  complete(
    date = seq(min(date), max(date), by = "day"),
    fill = list(openings = 0)
  ) |>
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    openings_smooth = as.integer(round(
      rollapply(openings, width = 3, FUN = median, align = "center",
        partial = TRUE)
    ))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(person_cov, by = "match_id") |>
  mutate(
    weekend = factor(
      if_else(wday(date, week_start = 1) %in% c(6, 7), "weekend", "weekday"),
      levels = c("weekday", "weekend")
    ),
    study_day = as.integer(date - min(date, na.rm = TRUE)),
    cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"),
    .by = match_id
  ) |>
  filter(age_ok)

4.9 Moderators and reference condition

Age, FOMO, and ostracism are z-standardized at the person level, so moderation effects are per SD. Control is the reference condition in all frames.

# Standardized moderators (per SD, person level).
mods <- person_cov |>
  transmute(
    match_id,
    age_z = z_score(if_else(age_ok, as.numeric(age), NA_real_)),
    fomo_z = z_score(fomo_mean),
    ostracism_z = z_score(ostracism_mean)
  )

add_mods <- function(frame) {
  frame |>
    select(-any_of(c("age_z", "fomo_z", "ostracism_z"))) |>
    left_join(mods, by = "match_id")
}

openings_daily <- openings_daily |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  add_mods()
dismissal_ev <- dismissal_ev |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  add_mods()
burst_daily <- burst_daily |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  add_mods()
burst_level <- burst_level |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  add_mods()

survey_long <- survey_long |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  left_join(mods, by = "match_id")
survey_pp <- survey_pp |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control")) |>
  left_join(mods, by = "match_id")

ctrl <- glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1e5, eval.max = 1e5))

5 Methods: Measures

Reliability, scree plots with parallel analysis, and one-factor confirmatory factor analyses with robust maximum likelihood estimation for FOMO (10 items) and ostracism (4 items; item 5 excluded).

pre_items <- pre

scale_reliability <- function(items) {
  alpha_val <- suppressWarnings(psych::alpha(items, check.keys = FALSE))
  omega_val <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(psych::omega(items, plot = FALSE))$omega.tot,
    error = \(e) NA_real_
  )
  tibble(
    n_items = ncol(items),
    alpha = round(alpha_val$total$raw_alpha, 2),
    omega_total = round(omega_val, 2)
  )
}

scale_prefixes <- c(
  FOMO = "fomo_",
  Ostracism = "ostracism_"
)

imap(scale_prefixes, function(prefix, scale_name) {
  items <- pre_items |>
    select(matches(paste0("^", prefix, "\\d+$"))) |>
    select(-any_of("ostracism_5"))  # item 5 excluded from every analysis
  scale_reliability(items) |>
    mutate(scale = scale_name, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()
## # A tibble: 2 × 4
##   scale     n_items alpha omega_total
##   <chr>       <int> <dbl>       <dbl>
## 1 FOMO           10  0.83        0.87
## 2 Ostracism       4  0.86        0.87
# Scree plots with parallel analysis. Ostracism excludes item 5.
scree_prefixes <- c(
  FOMO = "fomo_",
  Ostracism = "ostracism_"
)

scree_one <- function(prefix, scale) {
  items <- pre_items |>
    select(matches(paste0("^", prefix, "\\d+$"))) |>
    select(-any_of("ostracism_5"))
  invisible(capture.output(
    pa <- psych::fa.parallel(items, fa = "pc", plot = FALSE, n.iter = 100)
  ))
  tibble(
    scale = scale,
    component = seq_along(pa$pc.values),
    observed = pa$pc.values,
    parallel = pa$pc.sim
  )
}

scree_data <- imap(scree_prefixes, scree_one) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(scale = factor(scale, levels = names(scree_prefixes)))

ggplot(scree_data, aes(component)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = parallel, colour = "Parallel analysis"),
            linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = observed, colour = "Observed")) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed, colour = "Observed"), size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(vars(scale), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(max(scree_data$component))) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(Observed = "#9e0b1d", `Parallel analysis` = "#737373")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Component", y = "Eigenvalue", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

# One single-factor measurement model per scale.
items_for <- function(prefix, exclude = character()) {
  pre_items |>
    select(matches(paste0("^", prefix, "\\d+$"))) |>
    select(-any_of(exclude)) |>
    names()
}

one_factor <- function(name, prefix, exclude = character()) {
  paste0(name, " =~ ", paste(items_for(prefix, exclude), collapse = " + "))
}

cfa_models <- list(
  FOMO = one_factor("fomo", "fomo_"),
  Ostracism = one_factor(
    "ostracism", "ostracism_", exclude = "ostracism_5"
  )
)

cfa_fits <- imap(cfa_models, function(model, scale) {
  lavaan::cfa(model, data = pre_items, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")
})

fit_idx <- c(
  "chisq.scaled", "df", "pvalue.scaled", "cfi.scaled", "tli.scaled",
  "rmsea.scaled", "rmsea.ci.lower.scaled", "rmsea.ci.upper.scaled", "srmr"
)

imap(cfa_fits, function(f, scale) {
  m <- lavaan::fitMeasures(f, fit_idx)
  as_tibble_row(set_names(as.numeric(m), names(m))) |>
    mutate(
      scale = scale,
      n_items = sum(lavaan::parameterEstimates(f)$op == "=~"),
      .before = 1
    )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
## # A tibble: 2 × 11
##   scale     n_items chisq.scaled    df pvalue.scaled cfi.scaled tli.scaled
##   <chr>       <int>        <dbl> <dbl>         <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 FOMO           10      462.       35         0          0.797      0.739
## 2 Ostracism       4        0.755     2         0.686      1          1.00 
## # ℹ 4 more variables: rmsea.scaled <dbl>, rmsea.ci.lower.scaled <dbl>,
## #   rmsea.ci.upper.scaled <dbl>, srmr <dbl>
# Standardized loadings, one row per item.
imap(cfa_fits, function(f, scale) {
  lavaan::standardizedSolution(f) |>
    filter(op == "=~") |>
    transmute(scale = scale, item = rhs,
              loading = round(est.std, 2), se = round(se, 3),
              z = round(z, 2), pvalue)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

## 2       FOMO      fomo_2    0.83 0.022 37.26      0

## 6       FOMO      fomo_6    0.50 0.032 15.62      0
## 7       FOMO      fomo_7    0.40 0.037 10.80      0
## 8       FOMO      fomo_8    0.39 0.036 10.91      0
## 9       FOMO      fomo_9    0.21 0.043  4.98      0
## 10      FOMO     fomo_10    0.45 0.036 12.49      0
## 11 Ostracism ostracism_1    0.72 0.025 29.00      0
## 12 Ostracism ostracism_2    0.89 0.014 62.62      0
## 13 Ostracism ostracism_3    0.84 0.017 49.48      0

5.1 Intervention settings

Waiting prompts included a six-second animated pause by default, which participants could change in the app settings. Time planning prompts asked for the intended session duration. These chunks describe the waiting times and the self-set limits that participants actually used.

  count(limit_sec, sort = TRUE) |>

5.1.2 Waiting time (Waiting prompts)

# Waiting time per completed opening in the Waiting arm: 6 s by default, but
# participants could change it in the app settings.
wait_open <- behavior |>
  filter(
    cond == "Waiting",
    resolution == "openedApp",
    !is.na(intervention_duration)
  )

# Participants and openings with a waiting time other than the 6 s default
wait_open |>
  summarise(
    changed = any(intervention_duration != 6),
    n_open = n(),
    n_changed = sum(intervention_duration != 6),
    .by = match_id
  ) |>
  summarise(
    people_changed = sum(changed),
    people = n(),
    share_openings_changed = round(sum(n_changed) / sum(n_open), 3)
  )
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   people_changed people share_openings_changed
##            <int>  <int>                  <dbl>
## 1             19    172                  0.067
# Distribution of the waiting time across openings.
wait_open |>
  mutate(
    duration = case_when(
      intervention_duration < 6 ~ "1-5 s",
      intervention_duration == 6 ~ "6 s",
      intervention_duration <= 15 ~ "7-15 s",
      .default = "> 15 s"
    ),
    duration = factor(duration, levels = c("1-5 s", "6 s", "7-15 s", "> 15 s"))
  ) |>
  count(duration) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n), 3))

Sample sizes, the participant flow, age, balance across conditions, and the means, SDs, and correlations of Table 1.

6.1 Sample and condition balance

Number of participants per condition and analysis frame. The analyses of social media use include everyone who logged at least one decision point. The analyses of social media well-being include everyone who completed both surveys.

# Analyzable N per outcome frame and condition; N differs by inclusion rule.
count_people <- function(df, label) {
  df |>
    distinct(match_id, cond) |>
    count(cond, name = "n") |>
    mutate(frame = label)
}

) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cond, values_from = n) |>

6.2 Sample characteristics by condition (balance check)

Checks whether randomization produced comparable conditions in age, FOMO, and ostracism.

# Sample characteristics by condition
completer_ids <- survey_pp$match_id

tbl1_people <- openings_daily |>
  distinct(match_id, cond, age) |>
  left_join(
    person_cov |>
      select(match_id, fomo_mean, ostracism_mean),
    by = "match_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    completed = if_else(
      match_id %in% completer_ids,
      "Completed both waves",
      "Did not complete"
    ),
    condition = as.character(cond)
  )

cond_cols <- c("Overall", levels(tbl1_people$cond))

tbl1_all <- bind_rows(
  tbl1_people |> mutate(condition = "Overall"),
  tbl1_people
) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_cols))

cont_row <- function(df, var, label) {
  df |>
    summarise(
      cell = sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f)",
        mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .by = condition
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = cell) |>
    mutate(characteristic = label, .before = 1)
}

cat_rows <- function(df, var) {
  df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) |>
    count(condition, level = .data[[var]], name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      cell = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / sum(n)),
      .by = condition
    ) |>
    select(condition, level, cell) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = cell) |>
    rename(characteristic = level) |>
    mutate(characteristic = paste0("  ", as.character(characteristic)))
}

row_n <- tbl1_all |>
  count(condition, name = "value") |>
  mutate(value = as.character(value)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(characteristic = "N", .before = 1)

table1 <- bind_rows(
  row_n,
  cont_row(tbl1_all, "age", "Age, M (SD)"),
  cont_row(tbl1_all, "fomo_mean", "FOMO, M (SD)"),
  cont_row(tbl1_all, "ostracism_mean", "Ostracism, M (SD)"),
  tibble(characteristic = "Post-survey completion, n (%)"),
  cat_rows(tbl1_all, "completed")
) |>
  relocate(characteristic, any_of(cond_cols))

6.3 Exposure check

How many survey completers ever triggered the intervention? exposed is TRUE for anyone who logged at least one one sec event before the activity/scope filters. Completers who never did are excluded in the per-protocol sensitivity analysis (appendix).

exposure_check <- survey_pp |>
  distinct(match_id, cond) |>
  left_join(
    person_cov |> select(match_id, n_raw_events, exposed),
    by = "match_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    exposed = coalesce(exposed, FALSE),
    in_usage = match_id %in% openings_daily$match_id
  )

exposure_check |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    unexposed = sum(!exposed),
    exposed_in_usage = sum(exposed & in_usage),
    exposed_not_in_usage = sum(exposed & !in_usage),
    .by = cond
  ) |>
  arrange(cond)
## # A tibble: 3 × 5
##   cond         n unexposed exposed_in_usage exposed_not_in_usage
##   <fct>    <int>     <int>            <int>                <int>
## 1 Control    104         9               94                    1
## 2 Waiting    101         7               93                    1
## 3 Planning   106        11               88                    7
exposure_check |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    unexposed = sum(!exposed),
    pct_unexposed = round(100 * mean(!exposed), 1)
  )
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##       n unexposed pct_unexposed

6.4 Survey descriptives

Means and SDs of the well-being items by condition and wave, and the overall values reported in the Measures section.

# Pre/post evaluations: mean (SD) by outcome x condition x wave.
survey_long |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>

  as.character(cut(

    c("***", "**", "*", "")
  ))
}

7 RQ1: Effects on usage patterns

RQ1 asks whether waiting prompts and time planning prompts reduce social media use. We analyzed daily openings with negative-binomial GLMMs, dismissal of app use with logistic GLMMs, and daily burst rates with zero-truncated negative-binomial models. All models include the condition, a weekend effect, and a condition-specific study-day trend (natural cubic spline), with random intercepts for participants and, for daily openings and dismissal of app use, for apps. Intervention effects are marginal contrasts with Control, evaluated at the average study day and averaged over weekdays and weekends.

7.1 Daily openings

Negative-binomial GLMM; the effect is an incidence rate ratio (IRR) vs. Control.

# Negative binomial: condition + condition-specific time trend + weekend,
# with person and app random intercepts.
m_open <- glmmTMB(
  openings ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = openings_daily
)
summary(m_open)

Predicted share of dismissed decision points per condition (average predicted probabilities with 95% CIs from 1,000 draws of the fixed effects).

pp_draws <- function(fit, data, grid, n_sim = 1000) {
  beta <- fixef(fit)$cond
  tt <- delete.response(terms(fit))
  x_of <- function(d) model.matrix(tt, model.frame(tt, d, na.action = na.pass))

  re <- ranef(fit)$cond
  re_part <- re$match_id[as.character(data$match_id), 1] +
    re$app[as.character(data$app), 1]

  draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_sim, beta, vcov(fit)$cond)

  grid |>
    mutate(pred = map(cond, \(lvl) {
      d <- mutate(data, cond = factor(lvl, levels = levels(data$cond)))
      x <- x_of(d)
      list(
        est = mean(plogis(re_part + drop(x %*% beta))),
        sim = apply(draws, 1, \(b) mean(plogis(re_part + drop(x %*% b))))
      )
    }))
}

# Predicted rates (in %) per condition.
pp_levels <- function(res) {
  res |>
    transmute(
      name,
      estimate = map_dbl(pred, "est"),
      conf.low = map_dbl(pred, \(p) quantile(p$sim, 0.025)),
      conf.high = map_dbl(pred, \(p) quantile(p$sim, 0.975))
    ) |>
    mutate(across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), \(v) round(100 * v, 1)))
}

set.seed(20260408)

main_grid <- tibble(cond = levels(dismissal_ev$cond)) |>
  mutate(name = cond)
main_pp <- pp_draws(m_dis, dismissal_ev, main_grid)

pp_levels(main_pp)

7.4 Table 3: Intervention effects on usage patterns

The contrasts of the three models in one table.

# Table 3: intervention effects vs Control (emmeans contrasts). 
obj_models <- list(
  `Daily Openings (IRR)` = m_open,
  `Dismissal of app use (OR)` = m_dis,
  `Daily Burst Rate (IRR)` = m_rate
)

# Latent-scale person ICC (logistic model only).
icc_person_logit <- function(m) {
  s2 <- vapply(VarCorr(m)$cond, \(x) as.numeric(attr(x, "stddev"))^2, numeric(1))
  v_app <- if ("app" %in% names(s2)) s2[["app"]] else 0
  s2[["match_id"]] / (s2[["match_id"]] + v_app + pi^2 / 3)
}

table3_col <- function(label) {
  m <- obj_models[[label]]
  eff <- emmeans(m, ~ cond) |>
    contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, type = "response", adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  rc <- intersect(c("ratio", "odds.ratio"), names(eff))[1]
  arm <- function(cn) {
    r <- eff[eff$contrast == cn, ]
    fmt_ci(r[[rc]], r$asymp.LCL, r$asymp.UCL, r$p.value)
  }
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients$cond
  e <- co["weekendweekend", "Estimate"]
  s <- co["weekendweekend", "Std. Error"]
  weekend <- fmt_ci(exp(e), exp(e - 1.96 * s), exp(e + 1.96 * s),
    co["weekendweekend", "Pr(>|z|)"])
  sds <- vapply(VarCorr(m)$cond, \(x) as.numeric(attr(x, "stddev")), numeric(1))
  tibble(
    term = c(
      "Waiting prompts", "Time planning prompts", "Weekend",
      "Study-day trend (condition-specific)",
      "SD (Participant)", "SD (App)", "ICC (person)", "Num. Obs."
    ),
    !!label := c(
      arm("Waiting / Control"), arm("Planning / Control"), weekend,
      "included (2 df/arm)",
      sprintf("%.2f", sds[["match_id"]]),
      if ("app" %in% names(sds)) sprintf("%.2f", sds[["app"]]) else NA_character_,
      if (grepl("(OR)", label, fixed = TRUE)) {
        fmt_r(icc_person_logit(m))
      } else {
        NA_character_
      },
      format(stats::nobs(m), big.mark = ",")
    )
  )
}

reduce(map(names(obj_models), table3_col), full_join, by = "term") |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table 3",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Intervention Effects on Social Media Use Relative to Control (RQ1)"
    ),
    stub = "term",
    note = paste(
      "Control is the reference condition. Condition-specific time trends were",
      "included in the analysis but omitted here for brevity.",
      "\\* *p* < .05. \\*\\* *p* < .01. \\*\\*\\* *p* < .001."
    )
  )

7.5 Figure 3: Daily openings over study days

# Day in study is per participant, limited to 42 days

traj <- openings_daily |>
  mutate(day_in_study = as.integer(date - min(date)), .by = match_id) |>
  filter(day_in_study <= 41) |>

fig_traj <- traj |>

  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.6, linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.12) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_colours, labels = cond_labels,
    name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cond_colours, labels = cond_labels,
    name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 42, by = 7)) +
  labs(x = "Day in study (per participant)",
    y = "Mean daily openings (per person)") +
  theme_house() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

fig_traj

8 RQ2: Effects on social media well-being

RQ2 asks whether the interventions improve social media well-being. For participants who completed both surveys, linear mixed models include the survey wave (pre vs. post), the condition, their interaction, and a random intercept for participants. The wave × condition term is the intervention effect: the difference in pre-to-post change between each intervention and Control (Table 4, Figure 5).

8.1 RQ2 coefficient models (Table 4)

Fits the model once per outcome; Table 4, the effect sizes, Figure 5, and the diagnostics reuse these models.

# The wave x condition model per outcome, fit once (REML) and reused for
# Table 4, the effect sizes, the diagnostics, and Figure 5.
rq2_models <- map(
  set_names(outcomes_a),
  \(oc) lmer(value ~ wave * cond + (1 | match_id), data = filter(survey_long,
    outcome == oc))
)
# Coefficients per outcome.
iwalk(rq2_models, coef_lmm)

8.2 Standardized effect sizes (RQ2)

d is the difference-in-differences divided by the pre-intervention SD of the outcome.

# Difference-in-differences 
prepost_d <- function(oc) {
  m <- rq2_models[[oc]]
  d <- filter(survey_long, outcome == oc)
  sd_pre <- sd(d$value[d$wave == "pre"], na.rm = TRUE)
  ct <- emmeans(m, ~ wave * cond) |>
    contrast(interaction = c(wave = "revpairwise", cond = "trt.vs.ctrl"),
      adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  tibble(
    outcome = oc,
    contrast = paste(ct[[1]], ct[[2]]),
    did = round(ct$estimate, 3),
    d = round(ct$estimate / sd_pre, 3),
    d_low = round(ct$lower.CL / sd_pre, 3),
    d_high = round(ct$upper.CL / sd_pre, 3)
  )
}

map(outcomes_a, prepost_d) |> list_rbind()
## # A tibble: 4 × 6
##   outcome                   contrast                     did     d  d_low d_high
##   <chr>                     <chr>                      <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 social_media_satisfaction post - pre Waiting - Cont… 0.018 0.027 -0.288  0.341
## 2 social_media_satisfaction post - pre Planning - Con… 0.243 0.353  0.041  0.664
## 3 prob_self                 post - pre Waiting - Cont… 0.124 0.186 -0.158  0.53 
## 4 prob_self                 post - pre Planning - Con… 0.007 0.011 -0.331  0.352

8.3 Table 4: Social media well-being before and after the intervention

Model-based means at pre and post with the change per condition, and the intervention effects as b and d.

lab4 <- c(
  social_media_satisfaction = "Social media satisfaction",
  prob_self = "Problematic social media use"
)
cond_lab4 <- c(
  Control = "Control",
  Waiting = "Waiting prompts",
  Planning = "Time planning prompts"
)

# Panel A: means at pre and post and the change (post - pre) per condition.
means4 <- imap(rq2_models, function(m, oc) {
  em <- emmeans(m, ~ wave | cond)
  change <- contrast(em, method = "revpairwise", by = "cond") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    select(cond, change = estimate)
  as.data.frame(em) |>
    select(cond, wave, emmean) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = wave, values_from = emmean) |>
    left_join(change, by = "cond") |>
    mutate(outcome = oc)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

print(means4)
## # A tibble: 6 × 5
##   cond       pre  post   change outcome                  
##   <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>                    
## 1 Control   1.93  2.08  0.145   social_media_satisfaction
## 2 Waiting   1.99  2.15  0.164   social_media_satisfaction
## 3 Planning  2.00  2.39  0.389   social_media_satisfaction
## 4 Control   3.04  2.91 -0.127   prob_self                
## 5 Waiting   2.92  2.92 -0.00310 prob_self                
## 6 Planning  2.92  2.80 -0.120   prob_self
panel_a <- means4 |>
  mutate(
    across(c(pre, post), \(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)),
    change = if_else(round(change, 2) == 0, "0.00", sprintf("%+.2f", change)),
    cond = cond_lab4[as.character(cond)]
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = outcome,
    values_from = c(pre, post, change),
    names_glue = "{outcome}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  select(cond, starts_with("social_media_satisfaction"), starts_with("prob_self"))

# Panel B: wave x condition terms (b) and the standardized effects (d).
effect_terms <- c(Waiting = "wavepost:condWaiting", Planning = "wavepost:condPlanning")

effects4 <- imap(rq2_models, function(m, oc) {
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients[effect_terms, ]
  es <- prepost_d(oc)
  tibble(
    cond = cond_lab4[names(effect_terms)],
    outcome = oc,
    b = fmt_ci(
      co[, "Estimate"],
      co[, "Estimate"] - 1.96 * co[, "Std. Error"],
      co[, "Estimate"] + 1.96 * co[, "Std. Error"],
      co[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
    ),
    d = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", es$d, es$d_low, es$d_high)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind()

panel_b <- effects4 |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = outcome,
    values_from = c(b, d),
    names_glue = "{outcome}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  select(cond, starts_with("social_media_satisfaction"), starts_with("prob_self"))

# Column labels (same for both outcomes) 
col_labels4 <- function(labs) {
  cols <- as.vector(outer(names(lab4), names(labs), paste, sep = "_"))
  set_names(map(rep(labs, each = length(lab4)), md), cols)
}

# Outcome spanner over the matching columns.
spanners4 <- function(g) {
  g |>
    tab_spanner(lab4[["social_media_satisfaction"]],
      columns = starts_with("social_media_satisfaction")) |>
    tab_spanner(lab4[["prob_self"]], columns = starts_with("prob_self")) |>
    tab_stubhead("Condition")
}

panel_a |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table 4",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Intervention Effects on Social Media Well-being: Pre-to-Post Change",
      "Relative to Control (RQ2)"
    ),
    stub = "cond"
  ) |>
  spanners4() |>
  cols_label(.list = col_labels4(c(pre = "Pre", post = "Post", change = "Change")))

8.4 Figure 5: Social media well-being

The standardized effects of Table 4 as a figure: (A) social media satisfaction and (B) problematic social media use.

# Social media well-being outcomes as standardized DiD vs Control.
pre_sd <- survey_long |>
  filter(wave == "pre") |>
  summarise(sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .by = outcome)

subj_eff <- map(outcomes_a, function(oc) {
  m <- rq2_models[[oc]]
  sdp <- pre_sd$sd[pre_sd$outcome == oc]
  emmeans(m, ~ wave * cond) |>
    contrast(interaction = c(wave = "revpairwise", cond = "trt.vs.ctrl"),
      adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    transmute(
      outcome = subj_label[[oc]],
      condition = factor(c("Waiting", "Planning"), levels = c("Planning",
        "Waiting")),
      est = estimate / sdp, lo = lower.CL / sdp, hi = upper.CL / sdp
    )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(outcome = factor(
    outcome,
    levels = c("Problematic use", "Social media satisfaction")
  ))
d_range <- range(c(subj_eff$lo, subj_eff$hi, 0))

wb_panel <- function(label, xlab) {
  eff_panel(filter(subj_eff, outcome == label), xlab, NULL, ref = 0,
    log_x = FALSE) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = d_range)
}

fig_wellbeing <- (wb_panel("Social media satisfaction",
  "Social media satisfaction") /
  wb_panel("Problematic use", "Problematic social media use")) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8)),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 16, 8)
  )

fig_wellbeing

9 RQ3a: Heterogeneity: Age

RQ3 asks whether user susceptibilities moderate the intervention effects. Each usage model is extended by condition × moderator, and each well-being model by wave × condition × moderator. The moderated model is compared with the same model without these terms using AIC and BIC.

9.1 Usage outcomes

builders <- list(
  `Daily openings` = build_openings,
  `Dismissal of app use` = build_dismissal,
  `Daily burst rate` = build_rate
)

age_fits <- map(builders, \(b) b("age_z"))

# Delta AIC/BIC for adding the condition x age block.
susc_age_obj <- imap(age_fits, function(fit, oc) {
  drop_fit(fit, "cond:age_z") |>
    mutate(outcome = oc, moderator = "age", .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(c(d_aic, d_bic), \(x) round(x, 1)))

12 Moderation coefficients (Tables 5–7)

# ratio: TRUE for the usage models (exponentiated to IRR/OR), FALSE for the 
# well-being models (unstandardized b).
# three_way: TRUE for the well-being models, where moderation is the
# three-way term wave × condition × moderator
inter_coef <- function(model, mod_token, ratio, three_way) {
  co <- if (inherits(model, "glmmTMB")) {
    summary(model)$coefficients$cond
  } else {
    summary(model)$coefficients
  }
  rn <- rownames(co)
  keep <- grepl("cond", rn) & grepl(mod_token, rn, fixed = TRUE)
  if (three_way) keep <- keep & grepl("wave", rn)
  co <- co[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  pcol <- intersect(c("Pr(>|z|)", "Pr(>|t|)"), colnames(co))
  pcol <- if (length(pcol)) pcol[1] else ncol(co)
  est <- co[, "Estimate"]
  se <- co[, "Std. Error"]
  tr <- if (ratio) exp else identity
  tibble(
    Arm = if_else(grepl("condWaiting", rownames(co)), "Waiting prompts",
      "Time planning prompts"),
    Estimate = fmt_ci(tr(est), tr(est - 1.96 * se), tr(est + 1.96 * se),
      co[, pcol]),
    p = fmt_p(co[, pcol])
  )
}

mod_block <- function(models, mod_token, mod_label, ratio, three_way, fit) {
  deltas <- fit |>
    transmute(
      Outcome = recode(outcome, !!!subj_label),
      `ΔAIC` = sprintf("%.1f", d_aic),
      `ΔBIC` = sprintf("%.1f", d_bic)
    )
  imap(models, function(m, oc) {
    inter_coef(m, mod_token, ratio, three_way) |>
      mutate(Moderator = mod_label, Outcome = recode(oc, !!!subj_label),
        .before = 1)
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    left_join(deltas, by = "Outcome")
}


mod_table <- function(df, has_mod) {
  df <- df |>
    group_by(Moderator, Outcome) |>
    mutate(
      across(c(`ΔAIC`, `ΔBIC`), \(x) if_else(row_number() == 1, x, "")),
      Outcome = if_else(row_number() == 1, Outcome, "")
    ) |>
    ungroup()
  if (has_mod) {
    df |>
      group_by(Moderator) |>
      mutate(Moderator = if_else(row_number() == 1, Moderator, "")) |>
      ungroup() |>
      select(Moderator, Outcome, Arm, Estimate, p, `ΔAIC`, `ΔBIC`)
  } else {
    select(df, Outcome, Arm, Estimate, p, `ΔAIC`, `ΔBIC`)
  }
}
bind_rows(
  mod_block(age_fits, "age_z", "", TRUE, FALSE, susc_age_obj),
  mod_block(age_prepost, "age_z", "", FALSE, TRUE, susc_age_subj)

13.1 Post-survey completion (attrition)

Completion by condition (Table A1) and a logistic regression of completion on condition, age, FOMO, and ostracism.

# Post-survey completion by condition.

m_attrition <- glm(

  family = binomial(),

)

13.2 Intervention effects at different moderator levels

The intervention effects relative to control at low (−1 SD), average, and high (+1 SD) levels of each moderator, from the moderation models of RQ3: usage outcomes as incidence rate ratios or odds ratios (Figure A1) and well-being outcomes as differences in pre-to-post change (Figure A2).

mod_levels <- c(-1, 0, 1)

# Usage: IRR/OR vs Control at each moderator level.
usage_at <- function(fit, mod) {
  emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ cond |", mod)),
    at = set_names(list(mod_levels), mod)) |>
    contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, type = "response",
      adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    rename_with(\(x) "est", any_of(c("ratio", "odds.ratio"))) |>
    transmute(
      arm = if_else(str_detect(contrast, "Waiting"), "Waiting prompts",
        "Time planning prompts"),
      level = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[mod]])),
      est, lo = asymp.LCL, hi = asymp.UCL
    )
}

# Well-being: difference in pre-to-post change vs Control at each level.
wb_at <- function(fit, mod) {
  emmeans(fit, as.formula(paste("~ wave * cond |", mod)),
    at = set_names(list(mod_levels), mod)) |>
    contrast(interaction = c(wave = "revpairwise", cond = "trt.vs.ctrl"),
      adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      arm = if_else(str_detect(cond_trt.vs.ctrl, "Waiting"), "Waiting prompts",
        "Time planning prompts"),
      level = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[mod]])),
      est = estimate, lo = lower.CL, hi = upper.CL
    )
}

mod_sets <- list(
  Age = list(usage = age_fits, wb = age_prepost, var = "age_z"),
  FOMO = list(usage = fomo_fits, wb = fomo_prepost, var = "fomo_z"),
  Ostracism = list(usage = soc_fits, wb = soc_models, var = "ostracism_z")
)

cond_eff <- imap(mod_sets, function(m, mod_name) {
  bind_rows(
    imap(m$usage, \(fit, oc) mutate(usage_at(fit, m$var), outcome = oc)) |>
      list_rbind() |>
      mutate(type = "usage"),
    imap(m$wb, \(fit, oc) mutate(wb_at(fit, m$var), outcome = subj_label[[oc]])) |>
      list_rbind() |>
      mutate(type = "wb")
  ) |>
    mutate(moderator = mod_name)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = mod_levels,
      labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")),
    arm = factor(arm, levels = c("Waiting prompts", "Time planning prompts")),
    outcome = fct_inorder(outcome),
    # Waiting slightly above, Time planning slightly below each level.
    y = as.numeric(level) + if_else(arm == "Waiting prompts", 0.15, -0.15)
  )

# One panel per moderator (rows) and outcome (columns).
plot_levels <- function(df, ref, log_x) {
  p <- df |>
    ggplot(aes(est, y, colour = arm)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    facet_grid(moderator ~ outcome, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = levels(df$level)) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`Waiting prompts` = col_waiting,
        `Time planning prompts` = col_planning),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_house(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
  if (log_x) p + scale_x_log10() else p
}

fig_mod_usage <- plot_levels(filter(cond_eff, type == "usage"), ref = 1,
  log_x = TRUE)
fig_mod_wb <- plot_levels(filter(cond_eff, type == "wb"), ref = 0,
  log_x = FALSE)

fig_mod_usage

fig_mod_wb

ggsave("figures/figA1_moderator_levels_usage.png", fig_mod_usage, width = 8,
  height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/figA2_moderator_levels_wellbeing.png", fig_mod_wb, width = 6.5,
  height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

13.3 Robustness of the effects on social media use

Robustness of the usage effects (Table A3). Each alternative model differs from the primary model only in the examined part.

# Arm contrasts vs Control on the ratio scale (emmeans)
arm_cells <- function(m, component = "cond") {
  em <- if (component == "cond") {
    emmeans(m, ~ cond)
  } else {
    emmeans(m, ~ cond, component = component) |>
      regrid(transform = "log")
  }
  d <- em |>
    contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, type = "response",
      adjust = "none") |>
    summary(infer = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  rc <- intersect(c("ratio", "odds.ratio"), names(d))[1]
  tibble(
    Arm = if_else(grepl("^Waiting", d$contrast), "Waiting prompts",
      "Time planning prompts"),
    cell = fmt_ci(d[[rc]], d$asymp.LCL, d$asymp.UCL, d$p.value)
  )
}
spec_row <- function(m, outcome, spec, component = "cond") {
  arm_cells(m, component) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Arm, values_from = cell) |>
    mutate(Outcome = outcome, Specification = spec, .before = 1)
}

# Intervention effects of a well-being model (difference in pre-to-post
# change vs. Control) as table cells
did_cells <- function(m) {
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  rows <- c("wavepost:condWaiting", "wavepost:condPlanning")
  pcol <- if ("Pr(>|t|)" %in% colnames(co)) "Pr(>|t|)" else ncol(co)
  est <- co[rows, "Estimate"]
  se <- co[rows, "Std. Error"]
  tibble(
    Arm = c("Waiting prompts", "Time planning prompts"),
    cell = fmt_ci(est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se, co[rows, pcol])
  )
}

# Blank repeated outcome labels.
blank_repeats <- function(df) {
  df |>
    group_by(Outcome) |>
    mutate(Outcome = if_else(row_number() == 1, Outcome, "")) |>
    ungroup()
}

13.3.1 Model specification (social media use)

A common study-day trend for all conditions instead of a condition-specific trend.

# Primary = condition-specific trend
m_open_add <- glmmTMB(
  openings ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2) + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = openings_daily
)
m_dis_add <- glmmTMB(
  dismissed ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2) + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  family = binomial(),
  data = dismissal_ev
)
m_rate_add <- glmmTMB(
  burst_rate ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2) + weekend + (1 | match_id),
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = burst_daily,
  control = ctrl
)

13.3.2 Cleaning (daily openings)

Daily openings without each participant’s first and last active day, and with a three-day rolling median.

# (1) Transition-day trim: each user's first and last active day dropped.
m_trim <- glmmTMB(
  openings ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = mutate(openings_daily_trim, cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"))
)
# (2) Three-day rolling-median openings.
m_smooth <- glmmTMB(
  openings_smooth ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = openings_daily_smooth
)

13.3.3 Burst threshold

Bursts defined with a gap of 2 or 10 minutes instead of 5 minutes.

# Re-derive bursts at 2 and 10 min and refit the primary burst-rate model.
burst_daily_at <- function(gap_mins, events = access_ev) {
  events |>
    filter(
      resolution %in% c("openedApp", "dismissedAppOpening"),
      age_ok
    ) |>
    arrange(match_id, timestamp) |>
    mutate(
      gap = as.numeric(difftime(timestamp, lag(timestamp), units = "mins")),
      new_burst = is.na(gap) | gap > gap_mins,
      burst_id = cumsum(new_burst),
      .by = match_id
    ) |>
    summarise(
      calendar_date = first(date),
      study_day = first(study_day),
      weekend = first(weekend),
      cond = first(cond),
      n_events = n(),
      .by = c(match_id, burst_id)
    ) |>
    filter(n_events >= 2) |>
    count(
      match_id, calendar_date, study_day, weekend, cond,
      name = "burst_rate"
    ) |>
    mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"))
}
burst_model_at <- function(gap_mins) {
  glmmTMB(
    burst_rate ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id),
    family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
    data = burst_daily_at(gap_mins),
    control = ctrl
  )
}
m_burst2 <- burst_model_at(2)
m_burst10 <- burst_model_at(10)

13.3.4 Covariates, hurdle model, and end-of-limit definitions (usage)

Models adjusted for age, FOMO, and ostracism, a hurdle model that models days without completed openings separately, and alternative definitions of the decision points at the end of a limit.

# Each primary model refit with age, FOMO, and ostracism as covariates.
adj_covs <- "age_z + fomo_z + ostracism_z"

adj_open <- glmmTMB(
  as.formula(paste0(
    "openings ~ cond + ", adj_covs,
    " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id) + (1 | app)"
  )),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = openings_daily,
  control = ctrl
)
adj_dis <- glmmTMB(
  as.formula(paste0(
    "dismissed ~ cond + ", adj_covs,
    " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id) + (1 | app)"
  )),
  family = binomial(),
  data = dismissal_ev,
  control = ctrl
)
adj_rate <- glmmTMB(
  as.formula(paste0(
    "burst_rate ~ cond + ", adj_covs,
    " + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id)"
  )),
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = burst_daily,
  control = ctrl
)
# According to the model check below, the NB2 model predicts more days without 
# openings than observed. A hurdle model fits zero days and the number of 
# openings on other days separately (Table A3, "Hurdle").
m_open_hurdle <- glmmTMB(
  openings ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend +
    (1 | match_id) + (1 | app),
  ziformula = ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id),
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = openings_daily
)
# Alternative definitions of the decision points at the end of a limit.
# All decision points included in all outcomes.
open_all <- openings_from(behavior) |>
  mutate(cond = fct_relevel(cond, "Control"))
m_open_all <- update(m_open, data = open_all)
m_rate_all <- glmmTMB(
  burst_rate ~ cond + ns(study_day, df = 2):cond + weekend + (1 | match_id),
  family = truncated_nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = burst_daily_at(5, behavior_ev),
  control = ctrl
)

# Dismissal of app use without the decision points at the end of a limit.
m_dis_access <- update(m_dis, data = filter(dismissal_ev, !end_of_limit))
bind_rows(
  spec_row(m_open, "Daily openings", "Primary model"),
  spec_row(m_open_add, "Daily openings", "Common study-day trend"),
  spec_row(m_trim, "Daily openings", "First and last active day excluded"),
  spec_row(m_smooth, "Daily openings", "Three-day rolling median"),
  spec_row(adj_open, "Daily openings", "Covariate-adjusted"),
  spec_row(
    m_open_hurdle,
    "Daily openings",
    "Hurdle",
    component = "response"
  ),
  spec_row(
    m_open_all,
    "Daily openings",
    "All decision points"
  ),
  spec_row(m_dis, "Dismissal of app use", "Primary model"),
  spec_row(m_dis_add, "Dismissal of app use", "Common study-day trend"),
  spec_row(adj_dis, "Dismissal of app use", "Covariate-adjusted"),
  spec_row(
    m_dis_access,
    "Dismissal of app use",
    "Decision points at the end of a limit excluded"
  ),
  spec_row(m_rate, "Daily burst rate", "Primary model (5-min gap)"),
  spec_row(m_rate_add, "Daily burst rate", "Common study-day trend"),
  spec_row(m_burst2, "Daily burst rate", "2-min gap"),
  spec_row(m_burst10, "Daily burst rate", "10-min gap"),
  spec_row(adj_rate, "Daily burst rate", "Covariate-adjusted"),
  spec_row(
    m_rate_all,
    "Daily burst rate",
    "All decision points"
  )
) |>
  select(Outcome, Specification, `Waiting prompts`, `Time planning prompts`) |>
  blank_repeats() |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table A3",
    subtitle = "Robustness of the Intervention Effects on Usage Patterns",
    left_cols = c("Outcome", "Specification"),
    note = paste0(
      "Estimates are rate ratios (daily openings, daily burst rate) or odds ",

      "completed openings. All decision points models include decision points ",

      "study days. ",
      "\\* *p* < .05. \\*\\* *p* < .01. \\*\\*\\* *p* < .001."
    )
  )

13.4 Sensitivity of the effects on social media well-being

13.4.1 Covariates and per-protocol sample

Well-being models adjusted for age, FOMO, and ostracism, and refit without the survey completers who never triggered the intervention (Table A4).

# Per-protocol: completers who logged at least one one sec event.
exposed_ids <- person_cov |>
  filter(exposed) |>
  pull(match_id)
pp_long <- survey_long |> filter(match_id %in% exposed_ids)

map(set_names(outcomes_a), function(oc) {
  adj <- lmer(
    as.formula(paste0("value ~ wave * cond + ", adj_covs, " + (1 | match_id)")),
    data = filter(survey_long, outcome == oc)
  )
  pp <- lmer(value ~ wave * cond + (1 | match_id),
    data = filter(pp_long, outcome == oc))
  did_cells(rq2_models[[oc]]) |>
    rename(`Primary model` = cell) |>
    left_join(rename(did_cells(adj), `Covariate-adjusted` = cell), by = "Arm") |>
    left_join(rename(did_cells(pp), `Per-protocol` = cell), by = "Arm")
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "Outcome") |>
  mutate(Outcome = recode(Outcome, !!!subj_label)) |>
  blank_repeats() |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table A4",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Robustness of the Intervention Effects on Social Media Well-being"
    ),
    left_cols = c("Outcome", "Arm"),

13.4.2 Ordinal models

Cumulative-link mixed models that treat the single items as ordinal (Table A5).

# Four-point single items, so an ordinal model as a check.
ord_cells <- function(m) {
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  rows <- c("wavepost:condWaiting", "wavepost:condPlanning")
  est <- co[rows, "Estimate"]
  se <- co[rows, "Std. Error"]
  tibble(
    Arm = c("Waiting prompts", "Time planning prompts"),
    cell = fmt_ci(
      exp(est),
      exp(est - 1.96 * se),
      exp(est + 1.96 * se),
      co[rows, "Pr(>|z|)"]
    )
  )
}

map(set_names(outcomes_a), function(oc) {
  d <- survey_long |>
    filter(outcome == oc) |>
    mutate(value = factor(value, ordered = TRUE))
  ord <- ordinal::clmm(
    value ~ wave * cond + (1 | match_id),
    data = d,
    link = "logit"
  )
  did_cells(rq2_models[[oc]]) |>
    rename(`Linear mixed model (b)` = cell) |>
    left_join(rename(ord_cells(ord), `Ordinal model (OR)` = cell), by = "Arm")
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "Outcome") |>
  mutate(Outcome = recode(Outcome, !!!subj_label)) |>
  blank_repeats() |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table A5",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Linear and Ordinal Models of the Intervention Effects on",
      "Social Media Well-being"
    ),
    left_cols = c("Outcome", "Arm"),
    note = paste0(
      "Estimates are the difference in pre-to-post change relative to control ",
      "with 95% CIs. The ordinal model is a cumulative-link mixed model (logit ",
      "link) with the same fixed and random effects as the linear model. ",
      "\\* *p* < .05. \\*\\* *p* < .01. \\*\\*\\* *p* < .001."
    )
  )

13.5 Minimum detectable moderation effects

Smallest three-way interaction (wave × condition × moderator) that the well-being models could detect with 80% power at α = .05. For a two-sided test, this is (1.96 + 0.84) × SE ≈ 2.8 × SE of the interaction term. It is also expressed in pre-intervention SD units of the outcome.

# Pre-wave SD per outcome, to express the MDES in SD units.
mdes_pre_sd <- survey_long |>
  filter(wave == "pre") |>
  summarise(sd_pre = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .by = outcome)

mod_specs <- c(Age = "age_z", FOMO = "fomo_z", Ostracism = "ostracism_z")

# Wave x condition x moderator model per outcome (same models as Tables
# 5-7); b and SE of both three-way terms.
mdes_one <- function(oc, moderator) {
  mod <- mod_specs[[moderator]]
  m <- prepost_fit(filter(survey_long, outcome == oc), mod)
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  terms <- paste0("wavepost:cond", c("Waiting", "Planning"), ":", mod)
  tibble(
    outcome = oc,
    moderator = moderator,
    arm = c("Waiting prompts", "Time planning prompts"),
    b = co[terms, "Estimate"],
    se = co[terms, "Std. Error"]
  )
}

mdes_tbl <- expand_grid(oc = outcomes_a, moderator = names(mod_specs)) |>
  pmap(mdes_one) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(mdes_pre_sd, by = "outcome") |>
  mutate(mdes = 2.8 * se, mdes_d = mdes / sd_pre)

mdes_tbl |>
  transmute(
    Outcome = recode(outcome, !!!subj_label),
    Moderator = if_else(arm == "Waiting prompts", moderator, ""),
    Condition = arm,
    `Observed b [95% CI]` = sprintf(
      "%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se
    ),
    `MDES (scale points)` = sprintf("%.2f", mdes),
    `MDES (SD units)` = sprintf("%.2f", mdes_d)
  ) |>
  blank_repeats() |>
  gt_apa(
    title = "Table A6",
    subtitle = "Minimum Detectable Three-Way Interactions for Social Media Well-being",
    left_cols = c("Outcome", "Moderator", "Condition"),
    note = paste0(
      "Observed *b* is the three-way interaction of intervention condition × ",
      "moderator × survey wave per *SD* of the moderators. MDES = minimum ",
      "detectable effect at 80% power (two-sided α = .05), calculated as 2.8 × ",
      "*SE* of the interaction term. *SD* units = MDES relative to the ",
      "pre-intervention *SD* of the outcome."
    )
  )

14 Model diagnostics

For each model, we plot the residuals (the differences between observed and predicted values) and test for overdispersion, and we examine how much of the variance lies between participants (variance components, ICC) and how much the models explain (pseudo-R²). Residuals are simulated with the DHARMa package; for dismissal of app use, they are averaged per participant.

14.1 Usage models

# DHARMa diagnostics for m_open, m_dis, m_rate. Dismissal residuals are
# aggregated to person level.
resid_df <- function(sim) {
  pred <- sim$fittedPredictedResponse
  tibble(resid = residuals(sim), pred_rank = rank(pred) / length(pred))
}

qq_panel <- function(df, label) {
  df |>
    slice_sample(n = min(nrow(df), 3000)) |>
    arrange(resid) |>
    mutate(theoretical = ppoints(n())) |>
    ggplot(aes(theoretical, resid)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      x = "Expected (uniform)",
      y = "Scaled residual",
      title = paste0(label, ": QQ")
    ) +
    theme_house(base_size = 11)
}

resid_panel <- function(df, label) {
  q_lines <- df |>
    mutate(bin = cut(pred_rank, breaks = 20)) |>
    summarise(
      x = mean(pred_rank),
      q25 = quantile(resid, 0.25),
      q50 = quantile(resid, 0.50),
      q75 = quantile(resid, 0.75),
      .by = bin
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(c(q25, q50, q75), names_to = "q", values_to = "resid")
  df |>
    ggplot(aes(pred_rank, resid)) +
    geom_bin2d(bins = 50) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey90", high = "grey30", guide = "none") +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
      colour = "grey60",
      linetype = 2
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = q_lines,
      aes(x, resid, group = q),
      colour = col_planning,
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Predicted (rank-transformed)",
      y = "Scaled residual",
      title = paste0(label, ": residual vs predicted")
    ) +
    theme_house(base_size = 11)
}

diag_plot <- function(model, label, group = NULL) {
  # Conditional simulation, except for person-aggregated residuals.
  if (is.null(group)) {
    glmmTMB::set_simcodes(model$obj, val = "fix")
    on.exit(glmmTMB::set_simcodes(model$obj, val = "random"))
  }
  sim <- simulateResiduals(model, n = 1000, plot = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(group)) {
    sim <- recalculateResiduals(sim, group = group)
  }
  df <- resid_df(sim)
  qq_panel(df, label) + resid_panel(df, label)
}

diag_plot(m_open, "Daily openings")

diag_plot(m_dis, "Dismissal of app use", group = dismissal_ev$match_id)

diag_plot(m_rate, "Daily burst rate")

# Dispersion check for the count outcomes.
disp_check <- function(model, label) {
  sim <- simulateResiduals(model, n = 250, plot = FALSE)
  d <- testDispersion(sim, plot = FALSE)
  tibble(
    model = label,
    dispersion = round(unname(d$statistic), 2),
    p = round(d$p.value, 3)
  )
}
bind_rows(
  disp_check(m_open, "openings"),
  disp_check(m_rate, "burst_rate")
)
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   model      dispersion     p
##   <chr>           <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 openings         1.69 0.2  
## 2 burst_rate       0.98 0.944

testZeroInflation(sim_open, plot = FALSE)

list(

  map(\(m) tibble(intercept = ranef(m)$cond$match_id[, 1])) |>

14.2 Variance components, ICC, pseudo-R² (usage)

# Random-intercept variances for every primary model.
re_vars <- function(model, label) {
  vc <- VarCorr(model)$cond
  tibble(
    model = label,
    group = names(vc),
    variance = round(vapply(vc, \(m) m[1, 1], numeric(1)), 3)
  )
}
bind_rows(
  re_vars(m_open, "openings"),
  re_vars(m_dis, "dismissal"),
  re_vars(m_rate, "burst_rate")
)
## # A tibble: 5 × 3
##   model      group    variance
##   <chr>      <chr>       <dbl>
## 1 openings   match_id    0.443
## 2 openings   app         0.126
## 3 dismissal  match_id    0.451
## 4 dismissal  app         0.246
## 5 burst_rate match_id    0.687
# Latent-scale person ICC for the binary dismissal outcome.
icc_latent_binary <- function(model, focal = "match_id") {
  vars <- vapply(VarCorr(model)$cond, \(m) m[1, 1], numeric(1))
  round(vars[[focal]] / (sum(vars) + pi^2 / 3), 3)
}
tibble(
  model = "dismissal",
  icc_person_latent = icc_latent_binary(m_dis)
)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   model     icc_person_latent
##   <chr>                 <dbl>
## 1 dismissal             0.113
# Nakagawa marginal / conditional pseudo-R^2 (MuMIn)
if (requireNamespace("MuMIn", quietly = TRUE)) {
  r2_row <- function(model, label) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        r <- MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(model)
        tibble(
          model = label,
          R2m = round(r[1, "R2m"], 3),
          R2c = round(r[1, "R2c"], 3)
        )
      },
      error = function(e) tibble(model = label, R2m = NA_real_, R2c = NA_real_)
    )
  }
  bind_rows(
    r2_row(m_open, "openings"),
    r2_row(m_dis, "dismissal"),
    r2_row(m_rate, "burst_rate")
  )
} else {
  message(
    "MuMIn not installed; skipping pseudo-R2. ",
    "Run install.packages('MuMIn')."
  )
}
## # A tibble: 3 × 3
##   model         R2m    R2c
##   <chr>       <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 openings    0.049  0.593
## 2 dismissal  NA     NA    
## 3 burst_rate  0.03   0.611

14.3 Social media well-being models

# Normal QQ and residual-vs-fitted per outcome.
survey_resid <- outcomes_a |>
  set_names(subj_label[outcomes_a]) |>
  map(function(oc) {
    tibble(
      fitted = fitted(rq2_models[[oc]]),
      resid = resid(rq2_models[[oc]])
    )
  }) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  mutate(outcome = fct_inorder(outcome))

wb_qq <- survey_resid |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq_line(colour = "grey50") +
  stat_qq(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantile", y = "Residual", title = "Residual QQ") +
  theme_house(base_size = 11)

wb_fitted <- survey_resid |>
  ggplot(aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Fitted", y = "Residual", title = "Residual vs fitted") +
  theme_house(base_size = 11)

wb_qq / wb_fitted

# Unconditional person ICC + Nakagawa pseudo-R^2 of the wave x condition model.
have_mumin <- requireNamespace("MuMIn", quietly = TRUE)
na_r2 <- matrix(NA_real_, 1, 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("R2m", "R2c")))

map(outcomes_a, function(oc) {
  d <- survey_long |> filter(outcome == oc)
  m <- lmer(value ~ wave * cond + (1 | match_id), data = d, REML = FALSE)
  r2 <- if (have_mumin) {
    tryCatch(MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(m), error = function(e) na_r2)
  } else {
    na_r2
  }
  tibble(
    outcome = oc,
    icc = icc_uncond(d),
    R2m = round(r2[1, "R2m"], 3),
    R2c = round(r2[1, "R2c"], 3)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
## # A tibble: 2 × 4
##   outcome                     icc   R2m   R2c
##   <chr>                     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 social_media_satisfaction 0.324 0.045 0.388
## 2 prob_self                 0.248 0.01  0.258

The diagnostics indicated adequate fit of the primary models; the remaining deviations (fewer days without openings, single-item response format) are addressed by the hurdle and ordinal models in Tables A3 and A5.
